BPM Justification: The devil's quadrangle is literally textbook BPM process-redesign vocabulary; adding a fifth dimension to it is a modification to a core BPM decision model, not an idea imported from outside the field.
This is a direct application of Rosemann and vom Brocke's own BPM capability framework, so by construction it's BPM capability assessment, independent of the green framing layered on top.

Cynefin's ordered/unordered distinction is a general sense-making framework, not a BPM method, and the chapter doesn't translate it into anything a process designer could apply to an actual model or notation - the BPM tie is mostly that the argument happens to be about processes.

The Balanced Scorecard itself is a general strategic-management instrument, not a BPM artifact, and the chapter's use of it stays at the level of linking strategy to metrics rather than changing any process model, task, or control flow.
This is a notation extension to process models themselves - adding emission attributes to activities the same way a modeler would add cost or duration - which is as structurally BPM as a method gets.

Building directly on a process-performance-management maturity model means this is BPM governance tooling repurposed for sustainability, not a sustainability framework that happens to mention processes.

This reads as enterprise performance-measurement-system theory (a controlling/BI concern) with sustainability and 'all architecture levels' as the framing; it doesn't engage with process models, task structure, or BPM notation specifically enough to call it more than generically relevant.

Energy consumption data is fundamentally an infrastructure/facilities metric; routing it through case management and KPI tools is a real integration point, but the underlying concern being measured isn't itself a process-model or task-design question.

Project selection and success criteria sit in project management, a discipline adjacent to but distinct from process execution; the six-core-elements table does list project management as a BPM capability area, which is the only reason I don't rate this lower.

A network platform for sharing environmental indicators across organizations is inter-organizational data architecture; nothing here is specific to how a business process is modeled, executed, or improved.
